points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 渥雷·索因卡1934年7月13日出生于尼日利亚西南部的阿贝奥库塔，约鲁巴族家庭。他的父亲是学校校长，母亲是商人。在这个传统与现代交织的环境中，索因卡接触了约鲁巴传统文化和西方教育。这段经历为他后来的文学创作奠定了文化基础，使他在作品中融合了非洲传统元素和西方现代主义手法。童年时期，他开始对戏剧产生浓厚兴趣，经常参与学校戏剧表演，这为他日后成为剧作家埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: Wole Soyinka was born on July 13, 1934, in Abeokuta, southwestern Nigeria, into a Yoruba family. His father was a school headmaster and his mother a trader. Growing up in this environment blending traditional culture with Western education, Soyinka was exposed to Yoruba traditions and modern schooling. This formative period provided the cultural foundation for his later literary works, which would blend African traditional elements with Western modernist techniques. During his childhood, he developed a keen interest in drama, participating in school performances, which foreshadowed his future career as a playwright.

points.title: 大学教育
points.description: 索因卡进入尼日利亚大学学院（现为伊巴丹大学）学习，主修英语、文学和希腊语。在此期间，他积极参与校园戏剧活动，并创作了第一部戏剧《沼泽地的居民》。1954年，他获得政府奖学金前往英国利兹大学继续英国文学研究。这段学术经历使他接触了西方戏剧传统，同时加深了他对非洲文化独特性的认识。大学教育阶段是索因卡文学创作的起点，他开始思考非洲身份与殖民文化的关系，这成为他日后作品的重要主题。
points.descriptionEn: Soyinka attended University College (now University of Ibadan), where he studied English, literature, and Greek. During this time, he actively participated in campus drama productions and wrote his first play, 'The Swamp Dwellers.' In 1954, he received a government scholarship to study English literature at the University of Leeds in England. This academic exposure to Western theatrical traditions, combined with his deepening awareness of African cultural uniqueness, shaped his early literary direction. His university years marked the beginning of his literary career, as he began contemplating the relationship between African identity and colonial culture, a recurring theme in his later works.

points.title: 戏剧创作与政治活动
points.description: 回到尼日利亚后，索因卡在伊巴丹大学和拉各斯大学任教，同时积极创作戏剧作品。这一时期他创作了《狮子与宝石》、《森林之舞》等重要剧作，讽刺殖民主义和非洲社会问题。1960年尼日利亚独立后，索因卡成为国家剧院的首任艺术总监，致力于发展尼日利亚戏剧艺术。然而，随着政治局势恶化，他开始批评腐败的军人政府。1965年，他因揭露选举舞弊而被短暂监禁。这段经历使他的创作更加政治化，开始将戏剧作为社会变革的工具。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Nigeria, Soyinka taught at University of Ibadan and University of Lagos while actively writing plays. During this period, he created significant works like 'The Lion and the Jewel' and 'A Dance of the Forests,' satirizing colonialism and African social issues. Following Nigeria's independence in 1960, Soyinka became the first head of the National Theatre, dedicated to developing Nigerian dramatic arts. However, as political deteriorated, he began criticizing the corrupt military regime. In 1965, he was briefly imprisoned for exposing election fraud. This experience politicized his work, leading him to use theater as a tool for social change.

points.title: 内战囚禁
points.description: 1967年尼日利亚内战爆发，索因卡因试图与比亚法拉领导人谈判而被联邦政府逮捕，未经审判被单独监禁近两年。在狱中，他秘密创作了大量诗歌和戏剧，包括著名的《狱中人》。这段极端的监禁经历深刻影响了他的人生观和创作风格，使他的作品更加关注人权、自由和正义。1969年获释后，索因卡流亡英国，在谢菲尔德大学和剑桥大学任教。这段经历使他成为国际知名的持不同政见者，也为他赢得了国际社会的关注和支持。
points.descriptionEn: With the outbreak of the Nigerian Civil War in 1967, Soyinka was arrested by the federal government for attempting to negotiate with Biafran leaders and was held in solitary confinement without trial for nearly two years. During his imprisonment, he secretly wrote numerous poems and plays, including the famous 'The Man Died.' This extreme experience profoundly influenced his worldview and writing style, making his work more focused on human rights, freedom, and justice. After his release in 1969, Soyinka went into exile in the UK, teaching at the University of Sheffield and Cambridge University. This period established him as an internationally known dissident and garnered attention and support from the international community.

points.title: 学术巅峰与诺贝尔奖
points.description: 1975年，索因卡返回尼日利亚，在伊费大学担任英语和戏剧教授。这一时期他创作了《死亡与国王的马夫》等重要作品，继续批判政治腐败和社会不公。1986年，索因卡成为第一位获得诺贝尔文学奖的非洲作家，表彰他'以广阔的文化视野和富有诗意的情感，深刻描绘了当代生活的面貌'。然而，随着尼日利亚军人政权加强镇压，索因卡于1994年被迫再次流亡。尽管面临政治迫害，他仍坚持创作和批评，成为非洲知识分子抵抗压迫的象征。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，影响遍及全球。
points.descriptionEn: In 1975, Soyinka returned to Nigeria and became a professor of English and Drama at the University of Ife. During this period, he wrote significant works like 'Death and the King's Horseman,' continuing to critique political corruption and social injustice. In 1986, Soyinka became the first African writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, awarded 'for a poetic drama of great luminance which fuses elements of entertainment with a tragic vision of the human condition.' However, as Nigeria's military regime intensified repression, Soyinka was forced into exile again in 1994. Despite political persecution, he continued to write and critique, becoming a symbol of African intellectual resistance against oppression. His works have been translated into numerous languages, influencing audiences worldwide.

supporter.zh: 索因卡被誉为'非洲文学巨人'和'尼日利亚国宝'。支持者认为他通过戏剧、诗歌和散文，成功将非洲传统与西方现代主义融合，创造了独特的文学形式。他勇敢的政治立场和对民主与人权的坚定捍卫，使他成为知识分子的楷模。作为诺贝尔文学奖得主，索因卡不仅提升了非洲文学的国际地位，更通过作品揭示了后殖民社会的复杂现实，为非洲文化发声。
supporter.en: Soyinka is hailed as 'a giant of African literature' and 'Nigeria's national treasure.' Supporters argue that through his plays, poems, and essays, he successfully merged African traditions with Western modernism to create a unique literary form. His courageous political stance and unwavering defense of democracy and human rights make him a role model for intellectuals. As a Nobel laureate, Soyinka not only elevated the international status of African literature but also revealed the complexities of post-colonial societies through his works, giving voice to African culture.

critic.zh: 批评者认为索因卡的作品过于精英主义，脱离普通民众的生活。他复杂的语言风格和西方文学引用使他的作品难以被大众接受。一些非洲民族主义者批评他过度依赖西方文学传统，未能充分发展非洲本土叙事形式。此外，他在政治上的立场也被质疑为摇摆不定，有时被视为与西方势力过于亲近，忽视了非洲本土的政治复杂性。
critic.en: Critics argue that Soyinka's work is too elitist and disconnected from the lives of ordinary people. His complex language style and Western literary references make his works inaccessible to general audiences. Some African nationalists criticize his over-reliance on Western literary traditions, failing to fully develop indigenous African narrative forms. Additionally, his political positions have been questioned as inconsistent, sometimes seen as too aligned with Western powers while overlooking the complexities of African politics.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，索因卡被定义为后殖民时代非洲知识分子的代表人物。他的作品既是文学成就，也是政治宣言，体现了非洲知识分子在全球化语境中的挣扎与抗争。索因卡的形象超越了单纯的作家身份，成为文化抵抗的象征。他的生平和创作反映了20世纪非洲的政治变迁和文化认同问题，使他成为研究非洲现代史和文学的重要窗口。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Soyinka is defined as a representative figure of post-colonial African intellectuals. His works are both literary achievements and political statements, embodying the struggles and resistance of African intellectuals in a globalized context. Soyinka's identity transcends that of a mere writer, becoming a symbol of cultural resistance. His life and work reflect the political changes and cultural identity issues of 20th-century Africa, making him an important window for studying African modern history and literature.

self.zh: 监狱不能囚禁思想，思想是自由的。
self.en: The prison cell cannot contain thought; thought is free.

others.zh: 索因卡用他的笔和声音，为被压迫者发声，他的作品不仅是文学杰作，更是人类尊严的宣言。
others.en: With his pen and voice, Soyinka speaks for the oppressed; his works are not only literary masterpieces but declarations of human dignity.
